correctness.rationale: Decompose Ab=alpha b+beta v with v a unit vector perpendicular to b. For white Gaussian sketches, X=Sb and Y=Sv are independent standard Gaussian vectors. Conditional on X, X·Y/||X|| is a standard normal with distribution independent of X, so H=1/c_F is alpha+beta times an independent normal/chi ratio. Its continuous density is positive at zero, giving almost sure well-definedness, the reciprocal tail 2f_H(0)/t and the exact p<1 criterion. Gaussian regression of X on W=SAb leaves an independent isotropic Gaussian with coordinate variance beta^2/gamma^2, yielding the shifted scaled Student law for c_G and p<s. These are marginal laws, not independence assertions. Norms of c times a fixed nonzero vector plus a fixed vector are comparable to |c| outside a bounded interval, so approximation, error and true residual have the same thresholds. The beta law for the ratio of independent chi-squares gives the sign probability; integrating h^{-1} on the positive side shows that dropping negative Ritz values leaves divergence. For s>2, E[1/chi_s^2]=1/(s-2); completing the true residual square gives equation (5). The separately computed s=3 example gives sign probability 0.0202596632, tail 4/(25*pi), and expected squared GMRES residual 0.4 versus optimum 0.2. Independent quadrature and a 20,000-draw direct-sketch check corroborated these finite formulas; finite random samples do not test moment divergence. I read the original proof, verification notes, code, requirements and recorded output without executing uploaded code. This check applies to the fixed finite-s, one-step, unconditioned exact-arithmetic Gaussian model with beta>0; the eigenvector boundary is exact for both solvers.
